subsection.title: Learning Objectives
subsection.p: After completing this section, you should be able to:

list.item: Represent subsets and proper subsets symbolically.
Compute the number of subsets of a set.
Apply concepts of subsets and equivalent sets to finite and infinite sets.

subsection.title: Exponential Notation
subsection.p: So far, we have figured out how many subsets exist in a finite set by listing them. Recall that in Example 1.11, when we listed all the subsets of the three-element set $$L = \left\{ {newspaper,\ magazine,\ book} \right\}$$ we saw that there are eight subsets. In Your Turn 1.11, we discovered that there are four subsets of the two-element subset, $$S = \left\{ {heads,\ tails} \right\}$$. A one-element set has two subsets, the empty set and itself. The only subset of the empty set is the empty set itself. But how can we easily figure out the number of subsets in a very large finite set? It turns out that the number of subsets can be found by raising 2 to the number of elements in the set, using exponential notation to represent repeated multiplication. For example, the number of subsets of the set $$L = \left\{ {newspaper,\ magazine,\ book} \right\}$$ is equal to $$2^{3} = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 8$$. Exponential notation is used to represent repeated multiplication, $$b^{n} = b \cdot b \cdot b \cdot \ldots \cdot b$$, where $$b$$ appears as a factor $$n$$ times.

note.p: The number of subsets of a finite set $$A$$ is equal to 2 raised to the power of $$n(A)$$, where $$n(A)$$ is the number of elements in set $$A$$: $${Number\ of\ Subsets\ of\ Set}\; A = 2^{n(A)}$$.
Note that $$2^{0} = 1$$, so this formula works for the empty set, also.

problem.p: Find the number of subsets of each of the following sets.

list.item: The set of top five scorers of all time in the NBA: $$S = {\left\{ {LeBron\ James,\ Kareem\ Abdul-Jabbar,\ Karl\ Malone,\ Kobe\ Bryant,\ Michael\ Jordan} \right\}\text{.}}$$
The set of the top four bestselling albums of all time: $$A = \left\{ {Thriller,\ Hotel\ California,\ The\ Beatles\ White\ Album,\ Led\ Zepplin\ IV} \right\}$$.
$$n(S) = 5$$. So, the total number of subsets of $$S\;\text{is}\; 2^{5} = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 32$$.
$$n(A) = 4$$. Therefore, the total number of subsets of $$A\;\text{is}\; 2^{4} = 16$$.
$$n(R) = 3$$. So, the total number of subsets of $$R\;\text{is}\; 2^{3} = 8$$.

note.p: Compute the total number of subsets in the set of the top nine tennis grand slam singles winners, $$T = \{\text{Margaret Court, Serena Williams, Steffi Graff, Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic,~}$$ $$\text{Roger Federer, Helen Wills, Martina Navratilova, Chris Everett}\}$$.

subsection.title: Equivalent Subsets
subsection.p: In the early 17th century, the famous astronomer Galileo Galilei found that the set of natural numbers and the subset of the natural numbers consisting of the set of square numbers, $$n^{2}$$, are equivalent. Upon making this discovery, he conjectured that the concepts of less than, greater than, and equal to did not apply to infinite sets.

Sequences and series are defined as infinite subsets of the set of natural numbers by forming a relationship between the sequence or series in terms of a natural number, $$n$$. For example, the set of even numbers can be defined using set builder notation as $$\left\{ a \middle| a = 2n\;\text{where}\; n\;\text{is a natural number} \right\}$$. The formula in this case replaces every natural number with two times the number, resulting in the set of even numbers, $$\left\{ 2,4,6,\ldots \right\}$$. The set of even numbers is also equivalent to the set of natural numbers.

subsection.title: Check Your Understanding
subsection.p: Every member of a __________ of a set is also a member of the set.
Explain what distinguishes a proper subset of a set from a subset of a set.
The __________ set is a proper subset of every set except itself.
Is the following statement true or false? $$A \subseteq A.$$
If the cardinality of set $$A$$ is $$n(A) = 10$$, then set $$A$$ has a total of ___________ subsets.
If every member of set $$A$$ is a member of set $$B$$ and every member of set $$B$$ is also a member set $$A$$, then set $$A$$ is ____________ to set $$B$$.

exercises.instruction: For the following exercises, list all the proper subsets of each set.

For the following exercises, determine the relationship between the two sets and write the relationship symbolically. $$D = \{ 0,1,2,\ldots,9\},$$ $$A = \{ 0,2,4,6,8\},$$ $$B = \{ 1,3,5,7,9\},$$ $$C = \{ 8,6,4,2,0\},$$ $$Z = \{ 0\},$$ and $$\varnothing$$
For the following exercises, calculate the total number of subsets of each set.

problem.p: $$\{\text{football, baseball, basketball, soccer, hockey, tennis, golf}\}$$

exercises.instruction: For the following exercises, use the set of letters in the word largest as the set, $$U = \left\{ \text{l, a, r, g, e, s, t} \right\}.$$

problem.p: Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equivalent, but not equal, to the set: $$\left\{ \text{l, a, s, t} \right\}.$$
Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equal to the set: $$\left\{ \text{l, a, s, t} \right\}.$$
Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equal to the set: $$\left\{ \text{a, r, t} \right\}.$$
Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equivalent, but not equal, to the set $$\left\{ \text{a, r, t, s} \right\}.$$
Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equivalent, but not equal, to the set: $$\left\{ \text{r, a, t, e, s} \right\}.$$
Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equal to the set: $$\left\{ \text{r, a, t, e, s} \right\}.$$
Find two three-character subsets of set $$U$$ that are equivalent, but not equal, to each other.
Find two three-character subsets of set $$U$$ that are equal to each other.
Find two five-character subsets of set $$U$$ that are equal to each other.
Find two five-character subsets of set $$U$$ that are equivalent, but not equal, to each other.

exercises.instruction: For the following exercises, use the set of integers as the set $$U = \mathbb{Z} = \{\ldots, - 2, - 1,0,1,2,\ldots\}.$$

problem.p: Find two equivalent subset of $$U$$ with a cardinality of 7.
Find two equal subsets of $$U$$ with a cardinality of 4.
Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equivalent, but not equal to, $$\{ 0,3,6,9,\ldots\}.$$
Find a subset of $$U$$ that is equivalent, but not equal to, $$\{ - 1, - 4, - 9, - 16, - 25,\ldots\}.$$
True or False. The set of natural numbers, $$\mathbb{N} = \{ 1,2,3,\ldots\}$$ , is equivalent to set $$U.$$
True or False. Set $$U$$ is an equivalent subset of the set of rational numbers, $$\mathbb{Q} = \left\{ {\left. \frac{p}{q} \right|p\text{~and~}q\text{~are integers and~}q \neq 0.} \right\}.$$
